# CUT THE FLOW

> CUT THE FLOW is a browser-based non-linear video editor (NLE) that runs entirely on the client
> side. Multi-track timeline, audio mixing, colour grading, text and shape overlays, an AI editing
> assistant, and frame-accurate export to MP4, WebM or MP3. Nothing is uploaded, no server is
> involved, no account is required.

## Key features

- **Timeline editing** — multi-track NLE: drag & drop, split, trim, ripple edit, J-cut, L-cut,
  insert edit, snap-to-grid, per-track mute / solo / volume.
- **Audio** — multi-track mixing, per-clip fades, audio unlinked from video, waveform display.
- **Export — exactly 3 formats, one engine each**
  - **MP4** — H.264 + AAC, the universal choice (mobiles, TV, YouTube).
  - **WEBM** — VP9 + Opus, smaller files at equal quality.
  - **MP3** — the timeline audio only, encoded with LAME (not re-encoded from a video codec).
  All three encode **offline, frame by frame**: the output does not depend on the machine speed,
  and audio and video stay aligned (measured drift: **0 ms**).
- **Colour grading** — lift / gamma / gain, saturation, contrast, temperature, filter presets.
- **Effects** — 12 clip effects (pixelate, blur, invert, shake, mirror, glitch, scanlines, VHS,
  grain, duotone, teal-orange, RGB split), fades and transitions.
- **Text & overlays** — custom fonts (TTF / OTF / WOFF), size, colour, position, optional shadow,
  animations, auto-generated subtitles.
- **AI assistant** — natural-language editing. **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by default**, plus
  OpenRouter, Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini. Speaks French and English.
- **Projects** — `.ctf` (project + media bundled) or `.json` (lightweight). Both record the app
  version and the export format, so a reopened project keeps its settings. Auto-save to
  IndexedDB; optional IPFS publishing via Pinata.
- **PWA** — installable, works offline through a service worker.
- **Large sources** — automatic proxy generation for 4K and above.

## Technical stack

- Pure client-side: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript ES2022 — no framework, no build step, no bundler.
- One page (`index.html`) and one main class (`CutTheFlow`, in `js/app.js`).
- APIs: Canvas 2D, WebCodecs (`VideoEncoder` / `AudioEncoder` / `VideoFrame`), Web Audio,
  MediaRecorder (fallback only), IndexedDB, Service Worker.
- Vendors shipped locally: JSZip 3.10.1, MP4Box.js 0.5.2 (patched), lamejs 1.2.1 (LAME 3.100).

## Quality — measured, not claimed

A permanent regression bench (`tools/regression/`) replays a **13-second, 5-track control edit**
(two videos, one photo, a title, a shape, two audio tracks) through the three export engines,
saves and reopens the project, then verifies the produced files with ffmpeg. Latest run —
**29 checks out of 29**:

- 390/390 frames in MP4 and in WebM, valid MP3;
- **0 ms** audio/video sync offset, identical in the three formats;
- **0 duplicated and 0 skipped** frames during frame extraction;
- no black frame at the clip boundaries;
- **0 frames differing** from the source (pixel-level fidelity);
- layer order, text and shape overlays present only inside their time range;
- both `.ctf` and `.json` reopen with the same 5 tracks / 7 clips and the same export format.

## Usage

Open the app in a modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari), drag media onto the window,
arrange clips on the timeline, apply effects and colour grading, optionally ask the AI assistant
to edit, then export to MP4, WebM or MP3. Everything happens on the device.

## Version

**3.10.1** — September 2026. Three rewritten export engines with frame-accurate offline encoding,
a permanent regression bench, sample-accurate MP3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash as the default AI model,
and a true-black interface.
